partAClaim.mechanism: stripTrailingFootnoteMarker generalized from 'begins with literal terminal punctuation' to 'a short digit run glued to any preceding character, guarded against splitting a real decimal number'. The old strict boolean signal-A-OR-signal-B gate replaced with isPlausibleByPositionalSignals, a SCORED evaluation of five weighted signals (PARAGRAPH_BREAK=3, SENTENCE_TERMINAL_PUNCTUATION=3, NOISE_DISCOUNTED=1, CLOSING_DELIMITER=1, AT_LEAST_ONE_NEWLINE=1) accepted at threshold 3.
partAClaim.ownSelfDisclosedLimitation: Part A's own honest self-assessment already discloses one residual gap on the false-negative side (a footnote digit glued to a plain word with no punctuation/bracket still scores below threshold and is rejected, deliberately, to avoid reopening a certified false-positive boundary). It does not discuss the inverse risk investigated here: whether the same scoring composition can now accept something it should not.

codeReadDirectly.method: Read lib/contract-model/compiler/stage-structure.ts in full at the audited commit (not Part A's JSON) before writing any test.
codeReadDirectly.keyObservation: isPlausibleByPositionalSignals computes `noiseDiscounted = withoutNoise !== before` (line ~619) purely as 'did stripping typographic noise change the `before` text at all' within a 200-char lookback window. Nothing in this computation, nor in precededByClosingDelimiter or precededByAtLeastOneNewline, requires that the discounted noise be causally connected to THIS candidate being a genuine heading boundary - it only requires that a footnote/page-marker-shaped digit run existed SOMEWHERE in the trailing 200 characters before the candidate, glued to whatever character preceded it, and that after stripping it, the residual text also happens to end in a closing quote/bracket and contains at least one newline. A wholly unrelated genuine footnote belonging to an entirely different, earlier sentence can supply this same evidence for a completely unrelated candidate that merely happens to sit on the very next physical line.

A real lettered clause '(a)' genuinely belonging to Section 6.08's own body follows.
constructions.targetsMechanism: NOISE_DISCOUNTED(1) + CLOSING_DELIMITER(1) + AT_LEAST_ONE_NEWLINE(1) = 3, meeting PLAUSIBILITY_SCORE_THRESHOLD, computed for the 'Section 6.09' candidate using noise that belongs entirely to the PRECEDING, unrelated Section 6.08 sentence.

assessmentOfPartAsClaim.whatPartAGotRight: The originally-frozen FINDING-1 falsification (a footnote digit glued directly to a bare closing paren/quote/bracket dropping a real ARTICLE or SECTION, with a child re-parented to null) is genuinely fixed. All 21 tests in Part A's own suite pass, and this audit's own fresh false-negative probes across the integer-section and bare-integer pattern families (never explicitly composed with footnote-adjacency in Part A's own suite) confirm the fix generalizes correctly on the false-negative side. The generalized stripTrailingFootnoteMarker noise CLASS and the Category-6 decimal-number guard both hold under adversarial pressure.
assessmentOfPartAsClaim.wherePartAsClaimOverreaches: Part A's own design record frames NOISE_DISCOUNTED as evidence that 'something is obscuring the true boundary character' for THIS candidate, and explicitly argues CLOSING_DELIMITER is 'never treated as standalone-sufficient' because 'nothing about the bracket itself tells the two apart' - correctly identifying the risk in the abstract, but the actual implementation of NOISE_DISCOUNTED does not check that the discounted noise is adjacent to and part of the SAME sentence/boundary as the candidate's own preceding text, only that stripping changed something within a 200-character lookback window. A genuine footnote belonging to a completely different, earlier sentence supplies the exact same weight. Because CLOSING_DELIMITER and AT_LEAST_ONE_NEWLINE are cheap, common properties of ordinary in-text citations sitting at a line start (word-wrapped prose routinely puts 'Section N.NN ...' at the start of a physical line without it being a heading - the same real-world shape Part A's own doc-comment for signal (B) and the original P1-10 gate were written to guard against), any document containing both an ordinary footnote/endnote reference AND a line-wrapped in-text section citation nearby is newly exposed to a false positive that did not exist under the pre-Part-A boolean gate (which had no NOISE_DISCOUNTED signal to misapply).

dispositionRationale: OPEN-1 is NOT closed. Part A's remediation correctly fixes the specific false-negative reproduction it inherited (a real heading dropped and its child re-parented to null when preceded by a footnote glued to a bare closing delimiter), and this audit's own fresh false-negative probes across untested pattern families confirm that fix generalizes honestly. However, the SAME scoring composition Part A introduced to achieve that fix (NOISE_DISCOUNTED + CLOSING_DELIMITER + AT_LEAST_ONE_NEWLINE = 3, meeting threshold) opens a new, freshly-constructed false-positive path: a genuine footnote marker belonging to an entirely unrelated, earlier sentence, sitting immediately before an ordinary in-text section citation that happens to begin a new physical line, launders that citation into a false top-level heading. This reproduces the exact 'rank-stack corruption' failure class OPEN-1 is named for - a real child node (a lettered clause genuinely belonging to the true enclosing section's own body) is silently re-parented away from its correct ancestor to the spurious node - via a false POSITIVE rather than the false NEGATIVE direction Part A's fix targeted, confirmed under two materially different punctuation/case/digit-width combinations and isolated via controls that show removing only the unrelated glued digit restores correct behavior. Recommended remediation (not applied, per this task's read-only-on-production-code constraint): require NOISE_DISCOUNTED to only contribute weight when the discounted noise sits in the SAME unbroken run of non-newline text as the rest of the evaluated boundary (i.e. the footnote/page-marker artifact and the closing delimiter/newline evidence must all describe the one physical line immediately preceding the candidate, not merely something within an arbitrary 200-character lookback window that may span an entirely different sentence).
